Hong Kong Open 2026: Full schedule, Indians in action, prize money, withdrawals and all you need to know
 Lakshya Sen leads India’s charge at the Hong Kong Open 2026. Here is everything you need to know: dates, venue, USD 500,000 prize money and the Indians in action.

 | Photo Credit: SHIV KUMAR PUSHPAKAR
 File Photo: Back-to-back champion Lakshya Sen leads India’s challenge at the Hong Kong Open, the final qualifying event for the BWF World Tour Finals.
 | Photo Credit: SHIV KUMAR PUSHPAKAR
 Lakshya Sen heads into the Hong Kong Open, the final qualifying event for the BWF World Tour Finals, sitting sixth with 74,180 points and looking to seal his place in the season-ending tournament.
 Q: When and where is the tournament, and what is the prize money? 
 It runs from November 17 to 22 at the Grand Hall of the Kai Tai Arena, with a total prize purse of USD 500,000.
 Q: Who are the Indians in the draw? 
 Men’s singles: Lakshya Sen, Kidambi Srikanth.
 Women’s singles: Anmol Kharb, Ashmita Chaliha, Isharani Baruah, Unnati Hooda, Devika Sihag, Rakhsitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj.
 Men’s doubles: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy/Chirag Shetty (5), Hariharan Amsakarunan/M.R. Arjun.
 Women’s doubles: Treesa Jolly/Gayatri Gopichand
 Mixed doubles: Dhruv Rawat/ Maneesha K, Dhruv Kapila/ Radhika Sharma
 Q: Who has pulled out? 
 Ayush Shetty and HS Prannoy have withdrawn from the men’s singles. P.V. Sindhu, Tanvi Sharma, Malvika Bansod, Mansi Singh and Aakarshi Kashyap have withdrawn from women’s singles.
 Q: What is Lakshya’s form going into the event? 
 After early exits at the World Championships and Asian Games, Lakshya Sen has revived his season with back-to-back titles at the Hylo Open and Japan Masters 2026, the latter following a comeback victory in the final. Sitting sixth in the BWF World Tour rankings with 74,180 points, he heads into the Hong Kong Open looking to secure his place at the season-ending World Tour Finals.
 Q: How did Lakshya fare here last year? 
 Last year, Lakshya Sen reached the final of the Hong Kong Open, beating Chou Tien-chen in the semifinals before going down 15-21, 12-21 to Li Shifeng in the title clash.
 Q: Why is the doubles line-up worth watching? 
 The Indian doubles contingent adds more medal hopes with Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty leading in the line-up, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand feature in the women’s doubles.
 Note: The entry list is as of November 16. More withdrawals are possible closer to the start of the competition.
